verdict.rationale: First-party docs cover every element of the story. Raspberry Pi 3 suitability shows low-resource operation. Linux, Windows, macOS, FreeBSD and Kubernetes are listed for OS coverage. x86, amd64, ARM, RISC-V 64 and PowerPC are listed for CPU architectures. SQLite, MySQL, PostgreSQL, TiDB and MS SQL are listed for database backends. Independent hands-on reports corroborate light resource use: a $5 VPS, an Atom x7 fitlet2, a 4GB RAM host, a USB stick and a single-binary deployment.

support.subject: As a devops-lead, I can run a self-hosted instance on low-resource hardware across multiple OSes, CPU architectures, and database backends

citations.quote: A Raspberry Pi 3 is powerful enough to run Gitea for small workloads.
it works across all the platforms and architectures that are supported by Go, including Linux, macOS, FreeBSD/OpenBSD and Windows on x86, amd64, ARM, RISC-V 64 and PowerPC
Offers seamless integration with leading databases, including SQLite, MySQL, PostgreSQL, TiDB, and MS SQL.
Universally compatible with diverse operating systems and environments, including Linux, Windows, macOS, FreeBSD, and Kubernetes. Compatible with multiple architectures, such as x86 and arm64.
Gitea performs well even on slow hardware (a fitlet2 with an Atom x7-E3950 and 16GB RAM)
